title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: What the editor tells you, corrected
summary: Kotlin Jump 1.42.14 corrects what the editor was telling you: an error on `android.R.string.ok`, a "class not found" on a FileProvider from AndroidX with a removal quick fix behind it, a dispatcher lens accusing `viewModelScope` of touching the View, a signature help highlighting the wrong parameter behind a named argument, and a few more. It also removes a small regression of its own: Go to Definition rebuilt the scope index on every call since 1.42.6.

highlights.title: No error on android.R, no removal of FileProvider
highlights.description: A qualified R (android.R.string.ok, a library's R) is outside the workspace index and was reported as an error. A component from AndroidX or Firebase was badged "class not found", grayed and offered for removal; only a class in a package the workspace declares can be missing now.

highlights.title: Lenses and hints that tell the truth
highlights.description: The dispatcher lens no longer accuses viewModelScope.launch(Dispatchers.IO) of touching the View, signature help highlights the parameter named at the cursor, an Rx subscribe() pairs with the dispose() of its Disposable, and nativeMain covers the ios targets in the KMP badges.

highlights.title: Go to Definition back at full speed
highlights.description: Since 1.42.6 Definition, References and Rename rebuilt the scope index on every call, ten times the old cost on the benchmark. One index per document is shared now; the numbers are at or below the previous ones.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Keeps Flow<User> readable in a hover's KDoc, does not cut val OPEN = "{" at the brace, and attributes a string to the right class when an expression-body composable precedes it.
Says "every minute" for */1 in the cron tooltip, and drops the "⏱ Debug" lens the testCodeLens description promised.
